text.p: - An Austrian or Italian can buy 40 percent more with their average monthly salary than the average Slovenian, a Slovenian economic institute said.
- The Slovenian government told union representatives it would support workers' benefits, in spite of its drive to improve the economic competitiveness of Slovenian firms.
- Parliamentary committees investigating alleged irregularities in several former public companies and local communities resume work on Tuesday after the summer break.

- Slovenia's largest hospital, the Klinicni centre, said it would not be able to meet the stringent cutbacks in the number of doctors on night duty demanded by general Insurance company ZZZS as part of its cost-cutting drive.
- Roof tile producer Salonit Anhovo hopes to get financial help from the government, enabling the company to switch to asbestos-free production.
- The majority of foreign workers in Slovenia come from former Yugoslavia, employment statistics showed.
- Drugs producers and traders said a new law on the sale of pharmaceuticals, which came into effect in February, should be changed to allow general shops to sell drugs over the counter.
